name: Austinornis
isnote: Once thought a pangalliform (Clarke 2004); Mayr (2014) argued it is a non-neornithine, perhaps Apatornis or Iaceornis.
sum: Late Cretaceous ornithuran from the Austin Chalk of Texas known from a partial tarsometatarsus.
holotype: A partial tarsometatarsus from the Austin Chalk.
biology: Not given in the sources used.
author: Clarke 2004

sources.text: Clarke, J.A. 2004. Morphology, phylogenetic taxonomy, and systematics of ''Ichthyornis'' and ''Apatornis'' (Avialae: Ornithurae). Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 286: 1–179. doi:10.1206/0003-0090(2004)286<0001:mptaso>2.0.co;2
Mayr, Gerald Marc. The origins of crown group birds: molecules and fossils. Palaeontology 57(2): 231–242. doi:10.1111/pala.12103
